projects.title: Inventory Expiry Management System
projects.summary: A full-stack app that tracks product expiry dates for businesses, with a dashboard, calendar, charts, and reports — deployed live.
projects.problem: Small businesses lose money on stock that expires unnoticed. Tracking expiry dates in spreadsheets doesn't scale and gives no early warning before it's too late to act.
features: Dashboard with at-a-glance expiry status across inventory
Calendar view and charts visualizing upcoming expiry dates
Exportable reports for stock review
Secure multi-user login with per-user data isolation
projects.architecture: A React + TypeScript front end talking to a Node.js/Express REST API, backed by SQLite. Queries are parameterized end-to-end to keep them injection-safe, and each user's data is scoped server-side rather than filtered only in the UI. The front end is deployed on Vercel and the API on Render.
projects.challenges: Designing per-user data isolation correctly at the API layer (not just the UI), and structuring the calendar/chart views so expiry risk is obvious at a glance rather than buried in a table.
projects.lessons: Learned how much of "secure by default" comes down to boring discipline — parameterizing every query and re-checking data scoping at the API layer instead of trusting the front end to hide what a user shouldn't see.
projects.impact: My most complete end-to-end project so far: designed, built, secured, and actually deployed to production rather than left running only locally.

projects.title: Campus Store Management System
projects.summary: Full e-commerce web application with admin and customer roles, order management, and secure authentication.
projects.problem: Small campus stores often rely on manual, error-prone stock tracking and have no self-serve way for customers to browse and order products online.
features: Product catalog with filtering, sorting, and pagination
Order management with automatic stock deduction on purchase
User authentication with BCrypt password encryption
Role-based access control separating admin and customer views
projects.architecture: Layered Spring Boot MVC application — Thymeleaf templates for server-rendered views, a service layer for business logic, Spring Data JPA repositories over MySQL, and Spring Security handling authentication/authorization at the route level.
projects.challenges: Keeping stock counts consistent when orders are placed concurrently, and designing role-based routes so admin-only actions are fully inaccessible to customer accounts rather than just hidden in the UI.
projects.lessons: Learned to separate authorization checks at the controller layer instead of trusting the UI to hide restricted actions, and how BCrypt salting protects stored credentials.
projects.impact: Coursework project demonstrating a production-style e-commerce flow end-to-end, from schema design to checkout logic.

projects.title: Study Tracker App
projects.summary: Academic task management app with dynamic partial-page updates and zero full page reloads.
projects.problem: Students juggling multiple courses need a lightweight way to track assignment status without the clunkiness of a full page reload on every update.
features: Full CRUD for study tasks
Enforced status transitions: PENDING → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED
KPI dashboard showing live task counts by status
Course-based task grouping
projects.architecture: Spring Boot backend serving HTML fragments via HTMX, so the browser swaps only the changed DOM section instead of reloading the page — combined with Thymeleaf fragments and a MySQL-backed task store.
projects.challenges: Enforcing valid status transitions server-side (not just disabling buttons in the UI) so the state machine can't be bypassed by a direct request.
projects.lessons: Got hands-on with the HTMX request/response cycle and why partial server rendering can remove the need for a heavier JS framework on simpler CRUD apps.
projects.impact: Demonstrates a modern server-driven UI pattern as an alternative to SPA frameworks for straightforward CRUD tools.

projects.title: Cybersecurity Defense Game
projects.summary: Interactive game where players defend a server by scanning and destroying malicious network packets.
projects.problem: Cybersecurity concepts like packet inspection can feel abstract to learners — a game framing makes the underlying logic tangible.
features: 3-level class inheritance hierarchy for packet/entity types
Finite state machine with 4 distinct game states
Two separate UI versions built to compare interaction models
Usability study run with 15 participants
projects.architecture: Built in Java with the Processing framework; game entities modeled with an inheritance hierarchy, and game flow controlled by an explicit FSM (menu, playing, paused, game-over).
projects.challenges: Designing a fair comparison between a data-driven UI (raw stats visible) and a simplified visual UI, then interpreting mixed usability feedback from participants.
projects.lessons: Direct experience running a small UI/UX study — recruiting participants, structuring tasks, and translating qualitative feedback into concrete interface decisions.
projects.impact: Combined OOP architecture with real user-testing methodology in a single project. Built as a team project — the linked repo is hosted under a teammate's GitHub account.

projects.title: UrbanBite Restaurant Platform
projects.summary: Full-stack restaurant ordering and management platform with customer and admin interfaces.
projects.problem: Independent restaurants need a simple ordering platform that separates the customer-facing menu/order flow from admin-side order and menu management.
features: Customer ordering flow with forms and modal dialogs
Admin interface for managing orders and menu items
Client-side JavaScript validation on all forms
Documented workflows for every user journey
projects.architecture: Classic PHP server-rendered pages with jQuery-driven modals and form interactions on the front end.
projects.challenges: Structuring form validation so it caught bad input before submission while keeping the UI unobtrusive.
projects.lessons: Practiced presenting technical work to a non-technical audience — explaining the problem, solution, and business value in a formal presentation.
projects.impact: Delivered as a complete platform with a formal stakeholder-style presentation, not just working code.

projects.title: Hospital Management Database
projects.summary: Relational database system to manage patient records, appointments, and billing.
projects.problem: Hospitals need a data model that keeps patient, appointment, and billing records consistent while preventing duplicate or contradictory data.
features: Full ER diagram covering patients, appointments, staff, and billing
Schema normalized from 1NF through 3NF
Data integrity constraints (keys, foreign keys, checks)
SQL queries written for operational reporting
projects.architecture: Relational schema designed first as an ER diagram, then normalized and implemented in MySQL with explicit constraints enforcing referential integrity.
projects.challenges: Balancing full normalization against query complexity for common reporting needs.
projects.lessons: Solidified how normalization trade-offs affect real query patterns, not just textbook theory.
projects.impact: Demonstrates database design fundamentals applied to a realistic, multi-entity domain.

projects.title: Task REST API
projects.summary: A Task REST API demonstrating clean RESTful endpoint design with Spring Boot.
projects.problem: Practicing REST API fundamentals with a real, runnable service rather than isolated exercises.
features: Full CRUD via GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
Clean separation of controller and service layers
JSON request/response handling
projects.architecture: Standard Spring Boot MVC layering: controllers handle HTTP concerns, services hold business logic, keeping endpoints thin and testable.
projects.challenges: Keeping controllers thin and pushing logic into the service layer instead of letting it leak into request handlers.
projects.lessons: Reinforced REST conventions and HTTP semantics (status codes, idempotency) in a working codebase.
projects.impact: A clean reference implementation used to practice API design before more complex projects.

projects.title: Multi-Table JPA Application
projects.summary: A multi-table database application demonstrating JPA entity relationships and JPQL queries.
projects.problem: Understanding how ORM entity relationships map to actual relational tables, beyond single-table examples.
features: Multiple related entities mapped via JPA annotations
One-to-many and many-to-one relationship mapping
Cross-table queries written in JPQL
projects.architecture: Hibernate as the JPA provider over MySQL, with entity relationships defined through annotations and queried via JPQL rather than raw SQL.
projects.challenges: Getting bidirectional entity relationships to map correctly without causing infinite serialization loops.
projects.lessons: Learned the practical difference between JPQL and native SQL, and when each is the right tool.
projects.impact: Reinforced ORM fundamentals used across the other Spring Boot projects.

projects.title: Security & Session Demo
projects.summary: A Spring Boot application demonstrating secure authentication and session management.
projects.problem: Understanding how login security and session state actually work under the hood, rather than treating auth as a black box.
features: User authentication flow with Spring Security
Session-backed protected routes
Login/logout lifecycle handling
projects.architecture: Spring Security configured to protect specific routes, backed by server-side session state.
projects.challenges: Getting protected-route configuration right so unauthenticated requests are reliably redirected rather than silently failing.
projects.lessons: Built a working mental model of the authentication filter chain in Spring Security.
projects.impact: Foundational security project that fed directly into the authentication design of later apps like the Campus Store system.

projects.title: Secure Task UI
projects.summary: A front-end interface project for a task management system focused on clean, usable UI.
projects.problem: Practicing front-end UI design decisions independently of backend complexity.
features: Clean task list interface
Interactive UI elements built with vanilla JavaScript
Layout focused on clarity and usability
projects.architecture: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with no framework dependency, focused purely on front-end interaction design.
projects.challenges: Designing a UI that stayed usable and uncluttered without leaning on a component library.
projects.lessons: Practiced core UI/UX principles — hierarchy, spacing, and feedback states — from first principles.
projects.impact: Sharpened front-end fundamentals used across every other project's UI.

projects.title: WordPress Service Stack
projects.summary: Containerized WordPress stack (CIS 395) with Docker, Nginx, and MariaDB.
projects.problem: Learning containerized service deployment hands-on rather than through theory alone.
features: Multi-container WordPress + MariaDB stack via Docker
Nginx configured as the front-facing web server
Bash scripts written for automated backups
Full architecture and setup documentation
projects.architecture: Docker Compose orchestrating separate WordPress, MariaDB, and Nginx containers, networked together with persisted volumes for data.
projects.challenges: Getting container networking and persistent volumes configured correctly so data survived container restarts.
projects.lessons: Learned containerization fundamentals — images vs. containers, volumes, and inter-container networking — through direct deployment rather than slides.
projects.impact: Course project (CIS 395) demonstrating applied cloud/virtualization fundamentals.
